title: Systems with Complex Eigenvalues
short: Real and imaginary parts give spiraling solutions.

blocks.html: When $A$ has complex eigenvalues $\alpha \pm \beta i$, the eigenvector method still works, but it produces complex solutions. As with complex roots of one equation, their real and imaginary parts are the real solutions, and they spiral.

If $A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}$ with $\lambda = \alpha + \beta i$ and $\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{a} + i\mathbf{b}$, then $$\mathbf{u}_1 = e^{\alpha t}(\mathbf{a}\cos\beta t - \mathbf{b}\sin\beta t),$$ $$\mathbf{u}_2 = e^{\alpha t}(\mathbf{a}\sin\beta t + \mathbf{b}\cos\beta t)$$ are real solutions, and $\mathbf{x} = c_1\mathbf{u}_1 + c_2\mathbf{u}_2$. Trajectories spiral in if $\alpha < 0$, out if $\alpha > 0$, and close up if $\alpha = 0$.

$e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$ $= e^{\alpha t}(\cos\beta t + i\sin\beta t)(\mathbf{a}$ $+ i\mathbf{b})$. Multiplying out, the real part is $\mathbf{u}_1$ and the imaginary part is $\mathbf{u}_2$. Because $A$ is real, the equation $(\mathbf{u}_1 + i\mathbf{u}_2)' = A(\mathbf{u}_1 + i\mathbf{u}_2)$ splits into a real part and an imaginary part that must each balance, so $\mathbf{u}_1$ and $\mathbf{u}_2$ are both solutions. The direction of rotation is easy to read without any of this: at the point $(1, 0)$ the velocity is the first column of $A$, so if $a_{21} > 0$ the motion turns upward there, counterclockwise.

blocks.title: Eigenvalues and rotation
steps: At $(1, 0)$ the velocity is $(-1, 2)$: moving up, so counterclockwise.

blocks.title: Solve with an initial condition
steps: For $\lambda = -1 + 2i$: $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = 0$ has first row $-2i v_1 - 2v_2 = 0$, so $\mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -i \end{bmatrix}$: $\mathbf{a} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$, $\mathbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$.
blocks.a: $x_1 = e^{-t}\cos 2t$, $x_2 = e^{-t}\sin 2t$: a point circling counterclockwise as it shrinks toward the origin

blocks.title: A center
blocks.a: closed loops (ellipses), traversed clockwise with period $\pi$

blocks.html: Judging stability from $\beta$ or from the eigenvector. Only the real part $\alpha$ (half the trace) decides spiral in or out; $\beta$ sets how fast it turns. And the direction of rotation is not in the eigenvalue's sign of $\beta$: check the velocity at one point.
